Sealing is the stage
most cleaners skip

A sealed surface sheds oil, water and biological growth instead of drinking them. It is the difference between cleaning a driveway every summer and cleaning it once every few years. Penetrating, topical, colour and anti slip systems for concrete, aggregate, pavers and stone.

  • Three to seven years depending on the system
  • Applied on a clean dry surface, never same day
  • Quoted per square metre, separately from cleaning
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Sealing and surface protection

What a sealer does

Concrete, aggregate, sandstone, bluestone and unsealed pavers are porous. They have open capillaries that pull liquid in and hold it. A sealer either fills those capillaries or puts a film over them, so what lands on the surface stays on the surface where it can be swept or hosed off.

That changes three things at once. Stains stop going in, so oil and rust become a wipe rather than a restoration job. Moisture stops sitting in the surface, so mould and algae lose the damp they need. And freeze, salt and chemical attack slow down, which matters most on newer slabs. What a sealer does not do is make a surface indestructible or hide what is already in it, which is why the sequence is always clean, then dry, then seal.

Which sealer

Four systems that do genuinely different things

Most quotes say "we will seal it" without saying with what. These are not interchangeable and the wrong one on the wrong surface is a problem to strip, not a finish to live with.

Service life figures are for a residential driveway in Melbourne conditions under normal traffic. A commercial hardstand is shorter. A shaded path is longer.
  How it works Finish Typical life Best for
Penetrating sealer Soaks into the capillaries and reacts inside the surface Invisible. The surface looks exactly as it did Five to seven years Driveways and paths where you want protection without changing the look
Topical sealer Forms a film across the top of the surface Satin to gloss, colours deepen noticeably Three to five years Exposed aggregate and decorative concrete where the wet look is wanted
Colour sealer A pigmented topical coat that recolours as well as seals Uniform colour, satin or gloss Three to five years Tired or patchy concrete where cleaning alone will not even it out
Anti slip sealer A topical system with an aggregate additive in the coat Satin with a fine texture underfoot Three to five years Pool surrounds, ramps, steps and anywhere wet underfoot

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Why the sequence matters

Clean, dry, then seal, with days in between

STEP 01

Clean it properly

Sealing over a dirty surface locks the dirt under the coating permanently. Every stain has to come out first, which is why sealing is quoted alongside a clean rather than instead of one.

STEP 02

Let it dry out

Two to three clear days in a Melbourne summer and considerably longer through winter. Sealing a damp slab traps the moisture, and a topical coat over it goes cloudy white. That is a strip and redo, not a touch up.

STEP 03

Test the surface

A water drop test tells us whether the surface is still porous enough to take a penetrating sealer, or whether something was applied before that has to come off first.

STEP 04

Apply and cure

Two coats on most systems, with the second going on once the first has pulled in. Foot traffic after a day, vehicles after three, and no sharp turning on the surface for a week.

What it actually buys you

Five years of not thinking about it

  • 5 to 7 yearsTypical service life of a penetrating sealer on a residential driveway before it needs reapplying.
  • 2 to 3 daysClear drying weather needed between the clean and the seal. Longer through a Melbourne winter.
  • Wipe, not a jobWhat an oil spill becomes on a sealed surface, as long as it is dealt with rather than left.
  • Years, not monthsHow much longer a sealed surface holds its appearance between cleans compared with an unsealed one.

When not to seal

Four situations where we will talk you out of it

The surface is already failing

Spalling, delamination, crazing or a slab that has lost its cream is a concrete problem. Sealing it puts a coating over a surface that is still coming apart underneath, and it fails with it.

The stain has not come out

A sealer over a stain is permanent. Whatever shadow is left when we seal is the shadow you have for the life of the coating, and getting at it afterwards means stripping the sealer first.

Something was applied before and nobody knows what

Incompatible systems peel. Where a surface has an unknown coating on it, the honest answer is a test patch and often a strip, not a fresh coat over the top.

Rising damp or a moisture source underneath

If water is coming up through the slab, a topical sealer traps it and blisters. Fix the moisture first. A penetrating sealer may still be an option, and we will say which.

Eleven protection pages

Pick the surface or the system

Concrete sealingThe general case: driveways, paths, slabs and alfresco areas. Driveway sealingThe surface that takes traffic, oil and the most weather. Paver sealing and re-sandingJoints refilled first, then sealed, which also locks the sand in. Exposed aggregate sealingWhere a topical coat deepens the stone and stops it shedding. Stone and bluestone sealingNatural stone, which is more porous than it looks and marks easily. Concrete colour sealingRecolouring tired or patchy concrete rather than replacing it. Anti slip sealingPool surrounds, ramps and steps, where grip is the point. Anti graffiti coatingMakes removal a wash rather than a chemical job on repeat targets. Protective surface coatingsSpecified systems for commercial and industrial surfaces. Concrete resurfacingWhen the surface is past sealing and needs a new wear layer. Epoxy flooring and coatingsGarage floors and commercial interiors with a hard wearing finish.

Questions

Asked before sealing a surface

How much does concrete sealing cost in Melbourne?

Sealing is priced per square metre and the number moves with the system. A penetrating sealer on a sound driveway is the cheapest option and the longest lasting. A colour seal is the most expensive because it is effectively a recoat that also has to look even.

It is always quoted separately from the clean, so you can see what the protection costs on its own and decide whether it is worth it for your surface.

How long does concrete sealing last?

Five to seven years for a penetrating sealer on a residential driveway, three to five for a topical or colour system. Commercial hardstand with vehicle traffic and turning is shorter. A shaded path that nothing drives on is longer.

Topical sealers tell you when they are going: the sheen dulls and water stops beading. Penetrating sealers give no visual warning, so the water drop test is the way to check them.

Will sealing make my driveway slippery?

A gloss topical sealer can be slippery when wet, which is exactly why anti slip systems exist. For a driveway on a slope, steps, a pool surround or anywhere people walk barefoot and wet, we use a sealer with an aggregate additive in the coat.

A penetrating sealer does not change the surface texture at all, so it cannot make anything more slippery. Where grip matters and the look does not, it is the safest choice.

Can you seal straight after cleaning?

No, and anyone who offers to is going to cost you the job twice. The surface has to dry right through, not just on top, which is two to three clear days in a Melbourne summer and often a week through winter.

Seal a damp slab with a topical system and the trapped moisture turns it milky white. That cannot be polished out. It has to be stripped and redone.

Does sealing stop mould and moss coming back?

It slows it down a long way rather than stopping it. Mould and algae need moisture held in the surface, and a sealed surface does not hold it, so there is far less for them to work with. On a shaded south-facing path under trees you will still see growth eventually, but it sits on the sealer and washes off instead of rooting in.

Can you seal pavers, and what happens to the joints?

Yes, and the joints are half the job. We refill the joint sand first, because an empty joint lets a paver rock and lets weeds through. The sealer then binds the surface of that sand so it does not wash out again in the next downpour. Paver sealing and re-sanding covers it properly.

What if my concrete was sealed years ago?

Then the first question is what with. An old topical coat that is peeling or cloudy has to come off before anything new goes on, because a fresh coat over a failing one fails at the same rate. An old penetrating sealer simply wears out, and the surface can usually be cleaned and resealed without stripping.

The water drop test sorts this in a minute: if water soaks in, the old sealer has gone and the surface is ready. If it beads, it is still working and you do not need us yet.

Clean it once, then keep it

Sheds what it used to drink
